rule: Ensure motivation, ability, and a prompt converge simultaneously for users to perform desired behaviors.
quote: Behavior happens when Motivation, Ability, and a Prompt come together at the same time.

rule: Use streak mechanics to drive daily habit formation; users reaching 7-day streaks show significantly higher retention.
quote: learners who reach a streak of 7 are 2.4 times more likely to continue using Duolingo the next day
finding: 2.4x higher Day-1 retention for users with 7+ day streaks

rule: Expect automaticity timelines to vary widely by behavior type and individual; exercise habits take longer than eating or drinking habits.
quote: The exercise median was 91 days, compared with 65 for eating and 59 for drinking.
finding: Exercise: 91 days median; eating: 65 days median; drinking: 59 days median

rule: Use if-then plans to automate goal-directed responses by forming strong associations between situational cues and actions.
quote: Implementation intentions are "if-then" plans that define in advance how a goal will be pursued when encountering critical situations.

rule: Delay push notifications by one to two minutes after screen-on detection to maximize user engagement.
quote: slightly delayed screen-on pushes—arriving one to two minutes after users turn on their screens—generate significantly higher engagement than instantaneous pushes
finding: Delayed notifications generated significantly higher engagement than instantaneous pushes

rule: Avoid delivering notifications with hyper-precise timing as excessive precision can reduce user receptivity and feel intrusive.
quote: hyper-precise timing can backfire: messages delivered too immediately may feel intrusive, while modest delays enhance receptivity
finding: Inverted-U relationship between temporal precision and user responsiveness

rule: Use cohort analysis to segment users by behavior and identify feature adoption patterns across user groups.
quote: we implemented a new cohorting feature that lets us break down data based on different groups of users

rule: Render UI before full data synchronization completes using minimum required state to prevent perceived application lag.
quote: Render UI before vehicle_state sync when minimum required state is present, instead of blocking on full refresh

rule: Compress time-to-first-value to under 5 minutes for elite products; industry median is 36 hours.
quote: elite SaaS delivers first value in under 5 minutes; the industry median is roughly 36 hours
finding: Elite SaaS products deliver first value in under 5 minutes vs. 36-hour industry median

rule: Build branching onboarding paths that tailor to user context and remove information barriers to reach activation quickly.
quote: We have several branching paths that tailor the experience to the user and what information they may have, such as a subscription key or an existing Peloton account. This flexibility allows us to make sure there is always a path forward, so the user can start working out as quickly as possible.

rule: Track which onboarding steps users skip to identify friction points that need redesign or clearer copy.
quote: We can track how many members are skipping onboarding steps rather than engaging with them to see how valuable each step is.

rule: Design for behavior change by ensuring motivation, ability, and a prompt converge at the same moment.
quote: Behavior (B) happens when Motivation (M), Ability (A), and a Prompt (P) come together at the same moment.

rule: Use variable-ratio reinforcement to create habit-forming behavior that persists even after rewards stop.
quote: Variable-ratio is the most persistent: it is the most resistant schedule to extinction of all four, which helps explain the pull of gambling.
finding: Variable-ratio schedules produce the highest resistance to extinction compared to fixed-ratio, fixed-interval, and variable-interval schedules.

rule: Reinforce behavior continuously during early learning; switch to partial reinforcement once the habit is established.
quote: Due to the behavior being reinforced every time, the association is easy to make, and learning occurs quickly. However, this also means that extinction occurs quickly after reinforcement is no longer provided.

rule: Avoid artificially difficult processes; do not obstruct users from completing their task or accessing information.
quote: obstruction (artificially difficult processes)

rule: Disclose all relevant information before users commit to a purchase or transaction; never conceal or delay material facts.
quote: sneaking (concealed relevant information)

rule: Display real currency equivalent alongside virtual currency prices to prevent spending confusion.
quote: The real cost in fiat currency is not shown in the item purchasing experience.

rule: Avoid decoupling payment from consumption to reduce users overspending.
quote: when it is 'decoupled', people may overspend

rule: Use discrete pagination or product numbering instead of infinite scroll for task-oriented shopping.
quote: online retailers should use discrete pagination or product numbering on continuous websites to enhance consumers' control and purchase confidence.

rule: Use gradually intensifying visual friction to sustain intervention effectiveness longer than one-time pop-ups.
quote: the visual gradual intervention sustained subjective ratings the longest
finding: Visual intervention sustained longest vs. pop-up lost impact quickly

rule: Show all fees and total price before the user commits time or effort; reveal costs upfront, not at checkout.
quote: Hidden costs involve obscuring or omitting additional fees, charges, or costs until the user is well into the purchasing or sign-up process
finding: Users shown fees upfront spent 21% less and were 14.1% less likely to complete purchase

rule: Never hide critical information in small text, low contrast, or unexpected locations; use consistent hierarchy and prominence.
quote: Hidden on the purchase screen was some small, low contrast text stating upgrades cannot be refunded. This text was the lowest contrast text on the page, and was difficult to see

rule: Recognize that repeated interruptions deplete attention as a tax, eventually forcing users to comply against their interests.
quote: Every time an app or a website interrupts the user with a request to do something, this depletes the user's time and attention. This is like a tax that the provider imposes

rule: Never display false low-stock messages or fake demand indicators to pressure hasty purchase decisions.
quote: displaying misleading messages about low stock levels or high demand

rule: Do not exploit the scarcity cognitive bias by creating artificial urgency around limited supply or exclusivity.
quote: By tapping into the scarcity cognitive bias, this deceptive pattern preys on users' natural tendency to assign more value to items that appear rare or exclusive

rule: Visually distinguish advertisements from native content and interface elements with clear, persistent labeling.
quote: These ads are often designed to look like interface elements, related articles, or other content that users might be interested in

rule: Never make ad download buttons or calls-to-action resemble actual product download buttons or primary actions.
quote: displaying advertisements with a prominent download button that closely resembles the actual download button for the desired software

rule: Never use derogatory, shaming, or guilt-inducing language in opt-out button labels or rejection options.
quote: opt-out button labels that are worded in a derogatory or belittling manner, making users feel bad about choosing not to engage

rule: Do not emotionally manipulate users by triggering guilt or shame to influence decisions they would not otherwise make.
quote: Confirmshaming works by triggering uncomfortable emotions, such as guilt or shame, to influence users' decision-making

rule: Present price, taxes, fees, and key features consistently across all compared products on the same view.
quote: Taxes and fees are included in two of the plan prices, but not included in the third. Since the taxes and fees are not shown for the third plan the user cannot deduce if it is better value or not

rule: Avoid infinite scroll, autoplay, pull-to-refresh, streaks, daily rewards, and variable rewards that exploit compulsive behaviour.
quote: patterns such as variable reward schedules, loot boxes, infinite scroll, pull-to-refresh, autoplay, streaks, daily rewards, playing by appointment, and social validation loops

rule: Never withhold or obscure information relevant to user decisions, especially costs or consequences of their actions.
quote: Sneaking involves intentionally withholding or obscuring information that is relevant to the user (e.g. additional costs or unwanted consequences)

rule: Never require users to complete undesired actions to access desired features; present optional actions clearly and separately.
quote: Forced action involves a provider offering users something they want - but requiring them to do something in return.

rule: Make rejection or skip options visually equal or more prominent than accept options; position them prominently, not hidden.
quote: The 'skip this step' link was relatively small and hard to notice, positioned at the bottom right.

rule: Show stale data indicators when background synchronization is in progress to maintain transparency.
quote: Show a stale data banner while syncing

rule: Train AI agents on existing knowledge and processes, then simulate conversations end-to-end before deployment.
quote: Start with the knowledge you already have, then train Fin on your processes and policies. Use AI-driven Simulations to test fully simulated customer conversations from start to finish

rule: Deploy AI agents across multiple channels so customers receive consistent responses wherever they contact you.
quote: Deploy Fin across phone, email, chat, Slack, and more so every customer receives accurate, personalized responses, wherever they reach out

rule: Centralize all support knowledge in one hub to measure content performance across every customer touchpoint.
quote: Centralize, manage, and optimize all of the information that powers Fin, human, and self-serve support. See how your content is performing across every touchpoint including Fin, Copilot and on your Help Center with detailed reporting

rule: Identify activation as a specific in-product behavior threshold, not signup or onboarding completion.
quote: An Aha moment is the in-product event where a user first experiences the core value of your product — the 'Now I get it' trigger that converts a trial user into a likely long-term customer. It is not signup, not onboarding completion, and not feature adoption.

rule: Approximately 75% of users churn in the first week if they don't achieve activation.
quote: ~75% of users churn in the first week if they don't hit activation

rule: Segment activation thresholds by user type; B2B products often require both individual user activation and team-level activation.
quote: Different user types may have different Aha moments. A B2B SaaS often has both a user Aha (individual finds value) and a team Aha (team workflow becomes embedded).

rule: Do not exploit psychological vulnerabilities through addictive design patterns that foster compulsive behavior; such practices face regulatory enforcement.
quote: Addictive Design The user interacts with the product excessively, because its design exploits psychological vulnerabilities to foster compulsive behaviour.

rule: Do not assume habit formation will reach completion within an observation period; exercise subgroup median exceeded the 84-day study window.
quote: The observation period was 84 days, while the exercise median estimate was 91 days. More than half of those 13 selected exercise participants therefore had model-estimated times beyond the observation window.
finding: exercise median 91 days vs. 84-day observation period; upper quartile 118 days

rule: Recognize that only 48% of participants with adequate data met full modeling criteria for habit formation in 84 days.
quote: That left 39 participants, 48% of those with adequate data, for whom the asymptotic curve was a 'good fit.'
finding: 39 of 82 participants (48%) had good curve fits; 43 did not meet criteria

rule: Expose cancellation prominently on the same interface where signup occurs; hiding it violates consumer protection law.
quote: typically involves hiding the cancellation option, requiring users to call customer services to cancel

rule: Complete subscription cancellation in seconds, not minutes; New York Times test showed 8 minutes of rep talk versus seconds for signup.
quote: In one test it took roughly 8 minutes of conversation with a customer services rep to successfully cancel a subscription
finding: Cancellation took 8 minutes via phone versus seconds to create subscription
